boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten campus-adjacent corridors, each anchored by a named destination with a directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: South Street: Penn Museum
cards.subtitle: South Street corridor at 33rd Street
cards.notes: Walk South Street to the museum entrance and plan around its current galleries or public programs; confirm admission options before you go.
cards.short_summary: A named museum destination at South and 33rd Streets.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn identifies the Penn Museum at 3260 South Street, at the intersection of South and S. 33rd Streets.
cards.source_title: Directions to the Department | Department of Anthropology
cards.access_notes: Museum hours and admission conditions can vary; check the museum before visiting.

cards.title: Walnut Street: World Cafe Live
cards.subtitle: Walnut Street corridor at 31st Street
cards.notes: Use the venue calendar to choose an all-ages performance or community program, then approach from Walnut Street at the listed address.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit live-music venue on Walnut Street.
cards.evidence_claim: World Cafe Live describes itself as a nonprofit independent venue for live music, education, and community engagement at 3025 Walnut Street.
cards.access_notes: Event availability, ticketing, and age policies vary by program; consult the venue calendar.

cards.title: 36th Street: ICA Philadelphia
cards.subtitle: South 36th Street corridor near Sansom Street
cards.notes: Enter at 118 South 36th Street and browse the exhibitions on view; the ICA’s official site states that admission is always free.
cards.short_summary: Free contemporary-art exhibitions on South 36th Street.
cards.evidence_claim: ICA Philadelphia is at 118 S. 36th Street and states that it is always free for all visitors.
cards.access_notes: ICA lists public hours Wednesday through Sunday; review current exhibition and visit information before heading over.

cards.title: 40th Street: The Rotunda
cards.subtitle: Walnut Street corridor at 40th Street
cards.notes: Check the public calendar for a film, music, poetry, theater, class, or lecture, then follow the path from Walnut Street to the entrance.
cards.short_summary: An all-ages public arts venue just off Walnut Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rotunda at 4014 Walnut Street books public arts and culture events including music, film, dance, theater, poetry, classes, and lectures; all ages are admitted.
cards.access_notes: Programs and any ticket requirements vary; verify the event listing before visiting.

cards.title: Woodland Avenue: The Woodlands
cards.subtitle: Woodland Avenue corridor at 40th Street
cards.notes: Enter from Woodland Avenue for a daylight walk through the historic landscape; leave by the gates before they close at dusk.
cards.short_summary: A historic landscape and cemetery across from the 40th Street Trolley Portal.
cards.evidence_claim: The Woodlands is at 4000 Woodland Avenue, directly across from the 40th Street Trolley Portal, and its gates are open from dawn until dusk.
cards.access_notes: Respect that this is an active cemetery; self-guided visits are during daylight gate hours.

cards.title: 30th Street: Cira Green
cards.subtitle: South 30th Street corridor at Chestnut Street
cards.notes: Take the elevator from the Cira Centre South garage and use the elevated park as a daylight outdoor stop; check its posted access details first.
cards.short_summary: An elevated park above the Cira Centre South garage.
cards.evidence_claim: Cira Green’s official FAQ identifies it as an elevated park in University City and directs visitors to the Cira Centre South Garage at 129 S. 30th Street.
cards.access_notes: Review current access and event information before visiting.

cards.title: Baltimore Avenue: Clark Park
cards.subtitle: Baltimore Avenue corridor at 43rd Street
cards.notes: Use the park’s paths, playground, court, or scheduled community market as a daytime stop along Baltimore Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A nine-acre public park with recreation amenities and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation describes Clark Park as a nine-acre West Philadelphia park with historic features, a basketball court, playground, community events, and a year-round farmers market.
cards.source_title: Clark Park Engagement Assistant position description
cards.access_notes: Market schedules and recreational programming vary; check current event information.

cards.title: Baltimore Avenue: Trolley Portal Gardens
cards.subtitle: Baltimore Avenue corridor at 40th Street
cards.notes: Pause at the 40th Street Trolley Portal and look for the seasonal, all-ages pop-ups that University City District programs there.
cards.short_summary: A garden public space at the 40th Street trolley portal.
cards.evidence_claim: University City District identifies Trolley Portal Gardens at 40th Street and Baltimore Avenue and programs free, family-friendly events there.
cards.source_title: Trolley Portal Gardens Events | University City District
cards.access_notes: The listed free pop-ups are seasonal; consult the current schedule for dates and times.

cards.title: Cuthbert Street: The Lawn
cards.subtitle: Cuthbert Street corridor at 37th Street
cards.notes: Use the seating and green space at 37th and Cuthbert, or time your stop for the listed food-truck, music, movie, fitness, or craft programming.
cards.short_summary: A one-acre public lawn with seating and recurring programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lawn at uCity Square is a public space at 37th and Cuthbert Streets with seating, green areas, and events including music, movies, fitness classes, crafts, and food trucks.
cards.access_notes: Individual events and food vendors may have their own costs and schedules.

cards.title: Market Street: Drexel Square
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor at 30th Street
cards.notes: Walk to the 30th and Market corner for a green outdoor pause beside the station; pair it with a transit arrival or departure.
cards.short_summary: A 1.3-acre community park across from 30th Street Station.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel University identifies Drexel Square as a 1.3-acre community park at the corner of 30th and Market Streets, directly across from 30th Street Station.
cards.source_title: Drexel and Brandywine Open Drexel Square
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor public park; check local conditions or scheduled events before visiting.
